hooks.text: Black holes are not actually cosmic vacuum cleaners.
Replacing the Sun with a black hole wouldn't swallow Earth.
One specific black hole spins 1,000 times every second.

title: The Black Hole Vacuum Myth
description: Black holes do not suck in everything around them. At a distance, their gravity is identical to any normal star of the same mass.

beats.text: Black holes are not actually cosmic vacuum cleaners.
beats.visual: artist concept of a black hole bending light from distant stars

beats.text: Swapping the Sun for a black hole wouldn't swallow Earth.
beats.visual: diagram comparing gravitational pull of Sun vs equal mass black hole

beats.text: Our planet would simply keep orbiting the dark, empty space.
beats.visual: illustration of Earth orbiting a dark stellar mass black hole

beats.text: Matter only falls in after crossing the event horizon.
beats.visual: artist concept of the event horizon and accretion disk
queries: black hole point of no return

beats.text: The Milky Way's central black hole weighs four million Suns.
beats.visual: Event Horizon Telescope image of Sagittarius A* at the galactic center
queries: Sagittarius A* Event Horizon Telescope photo

beats.text: Astronomers proved its mass by watching nearby stars orbit it.
beats.visual: diagram tracking stellar orbits around Sagittarius A* from Keck Observatory

beats.text: One specific black hole spins one thousand times every second.
beats.visual: artist concept of fast spinning black hole GRS 1915+105

beats.text: Even that monster doesn't act like a giant vacuum.
beats.visual: graphic comparing a household vacuum to black hole gravity
queries: black hole gravity vs vacuum comparison

better_than_last: Prioritized the debunking of a common myth in the hook and beat 2 to improve early engagement, while integrating the Sagittarius A* record into the middle beats.
